rationale: Round 1 compiled and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this candidate scales up aggressiveness: with only 481 text bytes and three functions, there is large size headroom, so BCF and FLA get the highest security weights to maximize control-flow confusion of the dominant main() (404 bytes), which is where essentially all reverse-engineering value lies. FLA is weighted highest for SecurityGain since flattening defeats static flow recovery, with a moderate RuntimeCost weight (0.5) because the random-number loop in this benchmark is hot and flattening's dispatcher overhead must stay acceptable. IBR is boosted (0.8 SecurityGain) to break basic-block-level static analysis, at moderate risk since it composes well with FLA. SPLIT and SUB remain inexpensive diversity multipliers that layer with the heavier passes. ICALL is kept at moderate weight: this program has few call sites, so the resistance gain is limited and its indirect-call risk is not worth pushing higher. IGV is omitted because with only a handful of globals in this tiny program it adds overhead with negligible resistance benefit.
